fixture.note: Synthetic. Paris, 21 June 1990, midday clock time. Sun in the 10th, well above the horizon: an unambiguous day chart. Anchors the sect unit test. Note clock noon in CEST is ~1.8h before solar noon, so the Sun is near but not on the MC.

mind.howYouThink: You notice wording, timing, and the missing link in an explanation. You can turn a loose question into clear steps, and you often think best by talking it through. You also register your reactions while you are explaining them, so a busy conversation can pull attention away from what you feel. mind.howYouDecide: You decide by opening a path and moving toward a workable answer, then revising it when new facts arrive. You do not need every detail settled before you begin, but you do need a clear next step. If someone asks you to cover a shared expense, you may quickly suggest a plan, then change the terms once you check who owes what. That pause helps you avoid taking responsibility for more than you meant to.
mind.howYouAreUnderstood: You make yourself understood by asking direct questions and naming the practical point. People can follow your reasoning because you explain what needs doing and why. houses.reading: You often build confidence by getting better at something in public, then letting your work speak for you. Clear explanations and useful decisions help you feel capable, but they can become the standard you use to judge yourself. Behaviour check: Notice whether you feel more settled after someone has understood your point.

You value steady income and prefer to earn through skills that deepen with time. Learning, teaching, or work that connects you with other places can support your finances. You are more likely to keep a promise when the terms are clear and realistic. Behaviour check: Check whether a recent money choice reflects what you truly value.

You ask direct questions when a conversation feels tense, and you can keep pressing until you reach the real issue. Acting on your own ideas about shared costs or obligations can create friction, so make room for another person’s answer. Behaviour check: Before sending a blunt message, ask what you still need to know.

Home feels better when friends and chosen family can come and go, and when your space makes room for belonging. You may put a lot of care into the people around you, sometimes before noticing what would make your own home comfortable. Behaviour check: See whether you have made time this week for a quiet routine at home.

You take pleasure seriously and may prefer hobbies that reward patience and practice. New ideas can interrupt a familiar routine, while uncertain plans can make it hard to relax into play. Give enjoyment a place in your schedule before other duties claim the time. Behaviour check: Notice whether you did something fun without needing it to be useful.

You are learning to make daily work fairer and more cooperative, rather than carrying every task through sheer discipline. A practical routine can support your enjoyment, but it should not turn every free hour into another obligation. Behaviour check: Pick one recurring task and ask whether someone else can share it.

You may find partners through friendship or shared hopes, and you tend to believe in what people could build together. Compassion helps you meet another person’s uncertainty, but it can leave your own needs unspoken. Behaviour check: In one close exchange this week, say plainly what you can and cannot offer.

You move quickly when a shared bill, debt, or difficult commitment needs attention. That courage can stop a problem from growing, but acting before everyone agrees may leave others feeling pushed. Behaviour check: Before making a shared-money decision, write down who is responsible for what.

You build your beliefs through careful study and trust knowledge that holds up over time. Travel, education, and teaching can bring real pleasure, especially when they connect with what you already value. Behaviour check: Notice which idea you have tested in practice, not just enjoyed discussing.

You are good at making complicated work understandable, and people can rely on you to explain what needs doing. When several demands arrive at once, you may answer before checking what you need. Behaviour check: Before accepting a new task, pause long enough to name its cost in time.

You can bring generous people together around a shared aim, and friends may open doors for your plans. You may also let group needs shape your schedule before checking whether you want to join in. Behaviour check: Look at your next group commitment and ask whether you chose it freely.

You can miss private tiredness while focusing on visible work, then need more solitude than you expected. Rest may feel easier when you stop trying to make it productive or explain it to anyone. Behaviour check: Set aside a short private break this week before exhaustion chooses it for you.

overview.headline: You build your life around making ideas clear and useful in work people can see.
overview.distinctive: You combine a strong public voice with a serious need to protect time for pleasure. You can explain an idea with ease, yet take your creative work and promises seriously rather than treating them as casual. That can make you dependable, but it can also turn enjoyment into another duty. You may move fast to solve a shared problem, especially when others need help, while another part of you wants to wait and see whether the plan will hold. Friends can bring real support and opportunity, but their needs can crowd your schedule if you do not say what you can offer. Your unusual balance is practical initiative with a strong brake around what you enjoy: you start readily, but you want proof that a commitment is worth keeping. You may do your best work when you give yourself room to explore an idea without promising an immediate result.
overview.temperament: The leading light is your sense of purpose: you want to do work that reflects what you know and lets others recognise your contribution. You are made of earth in how you value what is practical, steady, and worth maintaining. You run on cardinal habits: you start when something needs doing, then keep moving toward a result. You investigate first and commit second. You talk a problem through before deciding what you need. You are quick to act when shared money or promises are involved, then may find that someone else expected more discussion. Your mind and daily needs stay close together, so a busy workday can make it hard to tell whether you want to help or simply feel obliged to answer. You do best when you check the cost and set clear terms before taking responsibility.
overview.concentration: You tend to put your attention where your words and decisions can make a visible difference. When a problem needs explaining, you ask questions, gather details, and find a way to make the next step clear. You often keep thinking about work after the day ends, especially when someone still needs an answer. Play and private rest can wait while you handle what feels urgent. You may only notice the cost when you are tired or less patient than usual.

foundation.chartThesis: You put your questions, words, and decisions into work other people can see. Being understood matters to you, but public demands can crowd out what you need privately. You do best when your work leaves room for rest and play.
foundation.centralTension: You can act quickly when money or commitments are shared, then discover that others expected a slower decision. Your caution around pleasure and long-term promises protects your time. Your speed protects your ability to act before a problem grows.
foundation.dominantPattern: You lead by explaining, asking, and making decisions in public. Friends and partners can help you do that work, while a busy schedule can make their requests hard to separate from your own plans.

discoveries.opening: You can move fast when a shared problem needs action, yet you need time and clear terms before you can trust a promise. You may also find that what steadies you privately does not always fit the pace of your public work.

paradoxes.title: Fast Help, Lasting Cost
paradoxes.tension: When a shared bill, debt, or urgent commitment needs attention, you can take charge before everyone has agreed on the details. You want the problem handled, not left to grow. But your quick action can sound like a promise to carry more than your share. You may later resent the time or money involved, even though you chose to step in. You are generous with practical help, yet you need others to be just as clear about what they will contribute.
paradoxes.invitation: Give yourself one pause before you commit, especially when someone else’s money or needs are involved. Ask what is known, what remains uncertain, and who will handle each part. That brief check lets your courage stay useful without making you responsible for everything. You can become someone people trust to act and to set fair terms.

paradoxes.title: Careful Joy, Public Drive
paradoxes.tension: You take pleasure and affection seriously. You may prefer steady romance, a craft you can improve, or promises that have stood the test of time. Yet your days can pull you toward visible work, quick answers, and decisions made in front of other people. You can be disciplined about what you create while still feeling pressed to prove your usefulness. Rest and play may end up waiting until the work is done, even when the work keeps arriving.
paradoxes.invitation: Set aside time for pleasure before your schedule fills, rather than treating it as a prize for finishing everything. Choose a small commitment you can keep, such as a regular creative hour or an unhurried evening with someone you love. This helps you stay dependable at work without losing the parts of life you enjoy.

paradoxes.title: Quiet Needs, Visible Work
paradoxes.tension: You often notice what needs saying or fixing before you notice how tired you are. Talking through a problem can help you think, and people may come to rely on your clear answers. Meanwhile, private strain can stay easy to dismiss because it does not announce itself in public. You may keep working through a need for rest, then realise later that your patience, focus, or willingness to help has worn thin.
paradoxes.invitation: Try checking in with yourself before the next person gets your answer. Ask whether you have eaten, rested, and chosen the task freely. You do not have to withdraw from work or from people to make room for those needs. With practice, you can answer clearly and still leave enough of yourself for the evening.

superpower.text: You are quick to find the question that makes a muddled problem easier to handle. You explain your thinking plainly, then turn it into a decision people can act on. Others often bring you complicated work because you can sort the details without losing the point. You learn well by asking questions, comparing accounts, and saying what you have understood. That skill stays reliable because you can use it in public, where your words meet real needs and get tested. You do not need perfect certainty before you speak. You are strongest when you give people a clear answer and leave room to revise it as facts change.
superpower.title: Clear, Useful Answers

actions.why: It helps you find the useful point before you take on the whole problem.
actions.action: Write down the one question that would clarify a current work problem.

actions.why: It lets you check that your reasoning is clear enough to use.

growingEdge.text: You can keep your attention on the job long after your body has started asking for a pause. Talking through a concern often helps you understand it, but you may speak before you know what you need. Then you stay available, answer one more request, and notice the strain later. It is possible to catch this sooner, though it may feel awkward to stop before you have a polished explanation. Try naming a need while it is still small: time to think, a meal, or an hour without messages. That does not make you less reliable. It helps you give a more honest answer and keep your working pace sustainable.
growingEdge.title: Make Room for Need

actions.why: It gives you time to notice what you need before another request arrives.
actions.action: Block one hour this week with messages turned off.

actions.why: It lets you hear your own view before you commit.

chronicPattern.text: When money, responsibility, or another person’s commitment is involved, you can move before everyone has agreed on the terms. You may volunteer to solve the immediate problem, then find that the cost or obligation lasts longer than you expected. Generosity and urgency can make a vague promise sound settled. This pattern is hard to remove because decisive action is one of your strongest tools, and delay can feel like letting a problem grow. It is more manageable when you pause long enough to ask who pays, who decides, and what happens if plans change. You can still act promptly without taking responsibility for terms nobody has named.
chronicPattern.title: Fast Shared Decisions

actions.why: It makes the commitment clear before your quick yes becomes a bill.
actions.action: Before agreeing to a shared expense, ask who pays what and when.

actions.why: It gives both people something specific to check.
actions.action: Put one current agreement in a message, including what happens if plans change.

relationships.howYouLove: You feel secure when affection is steady and plans are kept. You show love by making time, sharing good things, and staying through ordinary days. You may say you want someone thoughtful and easygoing, but you are drawn to warmth, generosity, and people who make friendship feel like a place to belong. You need both real affection and room to take pleasure slowly.
relationships.theChallenge: You can move fast when a partner’s money, needs, or future plans are involved, then find you agreed before you understood the full cost. You may step in because you care, especially when someone you love is under pressure. Later, when the commitment takes more time or effort than expected, you pull back or get frustrated. That does not make your care false. It means you need a pause between wanting to help and promising what you can give.

relationships.whatPartnershipAsks: Partnership asks you to let friendship become a clear agreement, not an assumption that good intentions will cover every gap. You do well with people who make you feel included, but you still need to say what you can offer and what you cannot. Let shared plans grow through repeated, honest conversations. You are learning to stay generous without taking responsibility for another person’s whole life.

venus_trine_saturn.growth: Treating the ease as a resource to be invested rather than a comfort to rest in.
venus_trine_saturn.dynamic: Venus and Saturn. Venus is attraction, pleasure, taste, and the capacity to draw people in. Saturn is structure, limit, duration, and the discipline that makes things last. Two functions in signs of the same element flow into each other without resistance. What they do together comes easily, often so easily that it goes unnoticed and undervalued.
venus_trine_saturn.tension: Complacency. The gift is taken for granted, left undeveloped, or used as an excuse to avoid harder things.
venus_trine_saturn.behavior: Effortless talent. The two functions combine naturally and reliably.

jupiter_trine_pluto.growth: Treating the ease as a resource to be invested rather than a comfort to rest in.
jupiter_trine_pluto.dynamic: Jupiter and Pluto. Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Pluto is intensity, power, and transformation through what cannot be avoided. Two functions in signs of the same element flow into each other without resistance. mars_square_jupiter.growth: Accepting that the tension is permanent and building something out of it rather than trying to resolve it.
mars_square_jupiter.dynamic: Mars and Jupiter. Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Two functions in signs that share a mode but not an element push against each other. Neither yields easily, so the pressure is constant and productive: this is where effort is forced and skill is built.
mars_square_jupiter.tension: Recurring conflict, frustration, and the sense of being pulled two ways at once.
mars_square_jupiter.behavior: Hard-won competence. The friction has been turned into a driving engine.

mars_square_neptune.dynamic: Mars and Neptune. Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. mercury_sextile_mars.growth: Deliberately using the connection rather than waiting for it to act on its own.
mercury_sextile_mars.dynamic: Mercury and Mars. Mercury is how a person thinks, learns, decides and makes themselves understood. Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. Two functions in compatible signs support each other when asked. The connection is friendly and productive but not automatic: it is an opportunity rather than a given.
mercury_sextile_mars.tension: Underused. The help is available but not taken, so the opportunity goes quiet.
mercury_sextile_mars.behavior: The two cooperate readily and produce practical results with modest effort.

neptune_sextile_pluto.growth: Deliberately using the connection rather than waiting for it to act on its own.

Pluto is intensity, power, and transformation through what cannot be avoided. Two functions in compatible signs support each other when asked. The connection is friendly and productive but not automatic: it is an opportunity rather than a given.
neptune_sextile_pluto.tension: Underused. The help is available but not taken, so the opportunity goes quiet.

moon_conjunction_mercury.growth: Learning to feel which of the two is speaking, and to give each its turn.
moon_conjunction_mercury.dynamic: Moon and Mercury. The Moon is the body, the habits, and what makes someone feel safe. Mercury is how a person thinks, learns, decides and makes themselves understood. Two functions occupy the same place and act as one. Neither can be used without engaging the other, so their natures blend, for better or worse depending on how compatible they are.
moon_conjunction_mercury.tension: The two cannot be separated, so the difficulty of one contaminates the other and there is no clean way to use either alone.
moon_conjunction_mercury.behavior: The two work as a single combined strength, each amplifying the other.

jupiter_opposition_saturn.growth: Owning both ends instead of projecting one, and finding the position between them.
jupiter_opposition_saturn.dynamic: Jupiter and Saturn. Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Saturn is structure, limit, duration, and the discipline that makes things last. Two functions in opposite signs pull in opposite directions and can see each other clearly. The tension is external and relational: it tends to play out between the person and someone else, or as a swing between two extremes.
jupiter_opposition_saturn.tension: Polarisation. The person identifies with one side and meets the other in someone else, usually as conflict.
jupiter_opposition_saturn.behavior: Balance and perspective. Each side tempers the other and the person can hold both.

personalPlanets.sun: The Sun is the centre of identity and the sense of what one is for. Gemini is quick, curious, verbal, and interested in everything at once. The 10th is vocation, reputation, and what one is known for doing.
personalPlanets.mars: Mars is drive, assertion, and the capacity to cut through and go after something. Aries acts first, directly and fast, and sorts things out afterward. The 8th is shared resources, loss, inheritance, and what is not one's own.
personalPlanets.moon: The Moon is the body, the habits, and what makes someone feel safe. Gemini is quick, curious, verbal, and interested in everything at once. The 10th is vocation, reputation, and what one is known for doing.
personalPlanets.pluto: Pluto is intensity, power, and transformation through what cannot be avoided. Scorpio goes deep, holds on, and does not do anything by halves. The 3rd is the near world: siblings, neighbours, daily talk, and learning.
personalPlanets.venus: Venus is attraction, pleasure, taste, and the capacity to draw people in. Taurus is steady, sensual, slow to start and slower to stop. The 9th is the far world: belief, higher learning, travel, and meaning.
personalPlanets.chiron: Chiron marks a wound that becomes a source of skill and understanding for others. Pisces feels everything, blurs boundaries, and gives more than it keeps. The 7th is the other: partners, spouses, open rivals, and one-to-one bonds.
personalPlanets.saturn: Saturn is structure, limit, duration, and the discipline that makes things last. Capricorn is disciplined, ambitious, and plays the long game. The 5th is pleasure, creativity, children, and what one does for its own sake.
personalPlanets.uranus: Uranus is disruption, independence, and the sudden break from what was expected. Capricorn is disciplined, ambitious, and plays the long game. The 5th is pleasure, creativity, children, and what one does for its own sake.
personalPlanets.jupiter: Jupiter is expansion, confidence, generosity, and the sense that more is possible. Cancer protects, remembers, and holds close what it cares about. The 11th is allies, friends, groups, and hopes shared with others.
personalPlanets.mercury: Mercury is how a person thinks, learns, decides and makes themselves understood. Gemini is quick, curious, verbal, and interested in everything at once. The 10th is vocation, reputation, and what one is known for doing.
personalPlanets.neptune: Neptune is dissolution, longing, imagination, and the blurring of hard edges. Capricorn is disciplined, ambitious, and plays the long game. The 5th is pleasure, creativity, children, and what one does for its own sake.
personalPlanets.north_node: The North Node is the direction of growth: unfamiliar, uncomfortable, and worth it. Aquarius stands apart, thinks in systems, and cares about the group. The 6th is work, routine, health, and what must be maintained.
personalPlanets.south_node: The South Node is the default: what comes easily and what gets overused. Leo is warm, proud, generous, and needs to be seen doing it. The 12th is what is hidden: solitude, sorrow, secrets, and self-undoing.
